nodes.note: Curve parity and straight parity are independently discoverable: knowing that curves occur an even number of times does not establish straight parity without the grid-cycle length argument. Split these checkpoints, and keep the stronger signed-turn identity as a proof example unless it needs its own checkpoint.

Divisibility by four and impossibility of length eight are separate restrictions requiring different arguments. Split them so a solver who obtains the divisibility condition but misses the eight-piece obstruction can be localized accurately.

This combines the staircase construction with exactly two straights and the operation supplying arbitrary additional pairs of straights. A solver can discover the first without the second; separate the base family from the straight-extension lemma.

The alternating-tooth base construction and the elongation of an isolated tooth are separately discoverable steps. Split the two-straight comb family from the operation adding arbitrary pairs of straights.

review.end_note: Each END route supplies the attainable maximum counts, a realizing construction, and enough boundary-traversal information for a linear or expected-linear implementation.
review.key_note: N6, N8, and N10 specify the respective constructions and output rules, rather than merely giving optimal lengths.
review.hazards_note: The hazards cover cyclic encoding, separate inventory limits, and the relevant small all-curved degeneracy. These constructions need no floating-point arithmetic, and their lengths and coordinates remain within ordinary signed 32-bit range.
review.editorial_note: The reference's all-curved construction agrees with N5 up to symmetry, but its positive-straight constructions are not the west-tail staircase of N4, the cross-bud construction, or the comb. The graph lacks construction/count/simplicity claims for the two absolute-direction families selected by C modulo four: N^a W (SW)^q S^a E (NE)^q and N^2 (WN)^p W^b (SE)^(p+1) S E^(b-1). In particular, lengthening their opposite runs need not produce N4's polyomino, so a solver following the reference does not establish a complete existing END route.

nodes.note: A solver can establish even curve count without establishing even straight count, which additionally uses the parity of the cycle length. Split these two parity claims, keeping the signed-turn and bipartiteness arguments as supporting evidence.

Divisibility by four and impossibility of length eight are distinct obstructions: the former leaves eight entirely unresolved. Split them so a solver who proves divisibility but gets stuck on the exceptional case can be located accurately.

The balanced and offset staircase families are separate construction insights; finding the family for curves divisible by four does not supply the other even residue class. Split the two families into construction nodes feeding N12.
